decision.title: Node atomization describes once; the costs left are the atomic cell's (packet )

item.p: Whom it serves: every atomization of a node (coercion of node arguments to atomic types, comparisons, fn:data, string functions given nodes), first SchXslt's expand stage of EN 16931, where left node atomization at 3.19 x 10^9 instructions (6.7 %).

Profile (callgrind, release, at 47a1d9a33; 47.78 x 10^9): 2.71 million atomizations, every one of an untyped node: 2.03 million attributes and 0.68 million text nodes, but only 4,903 distinct nodes, most of them parentless (node 0 of a tree of their own), each atomized about 550 times. One atomization cost about 1,010 instructions in sxml_node_make_typed_value: two node descriptions (113 each), the content (54) and sxml_atomic_item_make (590: the cell from the allocator 283, UTF-8 validation 178, type resolution through the registry about 70), and later the cell's free. The common case the packet names was confirmed: one xs:untypedAtomic from the string value, without a sequence builder ( had removed it).

Mechanism (src/xdm_node.c, no new machinery): the string value takes the caller's described node, so a typed value describes its node once (the public sxml_node_make_string_value describes it itself); the walk over the text descendants of a document or element steps over each element's attributes by attribute_count (they are stored right after it, ) instead of describing them, never past the last descendant.
Not changed: outcomes, error codes, steps (atomization charges none), (the walk is the same loop).

Measured (callgrind instructions x 10^9, release, before at 47a1d9a33, after 365e4257b): SchXslt expand 47.780 to 47.463 (one description) to 47.452 (attributes skipped), -0.7 %, output byte-identical to s2.sch; tests/bench/coercion.xq 2.716 to 2.697 to 2.695 (-0.8 %); xmark-all 8.747 to 8.646 to 8.643 (-1.2 %; its 0.86 million atomizations are mostly text-only elements). Processor seconds (fastest of seven, interleaved, a shared machine): expand 6.28 to 6.40, coercion.xq 0.303 to 0.367, xmark-all 1.205 to 1.043, within the machine's noise. Conformance setup: the base commit and the change built alike (git archive snapshots, preset ), run one after the other on the same machine with TZ, LANG and LC_ALL unset (UTC, the C locale), from the snapshot root: sxml-qt4 run --spec=XP40 --format=json, sxml-qt4 run --spec=XQ40 --format=json, sxml-xslt-test run --format=json (default catalogs, no test list). XP40 32,785, XQ40 46,114 and XT40 12,185 passed in both: 0 outcomes differ, case by case. debug-gcc: 437 of 437 tests pass; clang-tidy clean.

Left, outside this packet's files (see "## Proposed"): the atomic cell itself, about 70 % of what an atomization still costs. A scratch experiment that resolved xs:string and xs:untypedAtomic without the registry in sxml_atomic_item_make (src/xdm_atomic.c) took the expand stage from 47.45 to 46.98 (-1.0 %, 6.8 million calls of about 70 instructions); UTF-8 validation of text the tree already holds as well-formed UTF-8 is 1.21 (2.5 %); cell allocation through the allocator 2.04 (4.3 %) plus the frees. A memo of typed values per item heap would remove most of the 3.2, since SchXslt atomizes few nodes many times, but the heap's live-cell counts, which many tests check, would then count the memo; per evaluation it needs the dynamic context, and the public sxml_node_value_request cannot carry it ().
